decisions.reason: The general connector-placement flexibility does not override the immediately preceding requirement that J_BAT remain on a short edge.
Connector-edge flexibility does not change the ESP32 module, full pin access, breakout pitch, or already-flexible breakout-hole placement.
The existing same-message MODIFY already records the enclosure's transition to one integrated board, while the prior enclosure adaptation rule already accommodates the finalized connector layout.
The existing same-message MODIFY already removes the obsolete interboard-connector sourcing strategy; connector-edge flexibility introduces no additional sourcing change.

The one-board redesign removes the sensor board's main-board input connectors, but the external I2C sensor modules still require 3.3V supply from the integrated board, so that supply key must be updated rather than deleted.

decisions.reason: The AXP power-path requirement already applies to the integrated board, and connector placement does not alter its electrical topology or charging behavior.
The existing same-message MODIFY already records removal of the modular interboard interface and deletes its obsolete connector and topology details.

The single-board design makes modular-board references potentially stale, but the source does not establish the integrated current-monitor topology or resolve whether the separate INA monitor is retained.
Flexible physical positioning of buttons and connectors does not change the panel-input GPIO assignments or the requirement to connect panel controls through board connectors.

With only one integrated board and no interboard cable path, the panel power-button connector necessarily moves from the modular main board to the integrated board and connects to the AXP2101 PWRON control there.
